concept.name: DeFi liquidity provider
concept.definition: A DeFi liquidity provider (LP) is a user who deposits tokens into an AMM liquidity pool (or lending pool) and in return holds a pro-rata claim on the pool's reserves and the fees those reserves generate.
concept.intuition: LPs are the inventory suppliers of on-chain markets: they rent out their tokens to the pool and get paid a cut of every trade — while silently selling winners and buying losers as prices move.
concept.mechanics: In Uniswap v2, depositing equal values of two tokens mints ERC-20 LP tokens tracking the provider's pool share, redeemable for reserves plus fees; in v3, LPs choose price ranges and receive NFT positions. LP returns equal trading fees plus incentive rewards minus impermanent loss from price divergence.
concept.failure_modes: Impermanent loss in trending markets can exceed fee income, leaving LPs worse off than holding; LP positions also inherit smart contract risk, and v3 ranges can drift out-of-range and earn nothing.
concept.misconceptions: LP'ing is not risk-free yield — it is a short-volatility position whose PnL = fees + rewards − impermanent loss. High APRs quoted from incentive tokens usually decay as more liquidity joins and token emissions fall.
concept.example: An LP supplying $5,000 of ETH and $5,000 of USDC to a 0.3%-fee pool with $1M daily volume and $10M TVL earns roughly 0.3%×$1M×(10k/10M) ≈ $3/day before considering impermanent loss.

citations.source: Chainlink - Understanding Impermanent Loss in DeFi Liquidity Pools
